title: review: Q1: orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py — decision taxonomy for Planner invocations (purpose over complexity), pure and testable (P2)
spec:
Why: decision.py routes points by kind (held/scouts_done/closable) and risk, but nothing names the PURPOSE of a Planner decision; the router (Q4), telemetry (Q2) and Planner scorecard (Q5) need a stable decision_type to group by (brief .orchestrator/planner-routing-program.md P2).
What: new pure module orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py; no bus reads, no config reads, inputs never mutated.
- DECISION_TYPES = ("initial_goal_plan", "scout_results", "held_task", "architectural_replan", "fix_strategy", "closable_goal", "retrospective", "ambiguous_requirement", "other").
- classify(point, ctx, *, goal=None, task=None) -> {"decision_type", "architectural": bool, "ambiguous": bool, "risk_class": "none"|"low"|"high", "signals": [str], "band", "task_class"}. point is planner_runs' dict {goal_id, kind, payload_key, task_id?}; ctx is decision.route's ctx (see orchestrator/decision.py docstring and planner_runs.build_ctx lines 1002-1062); goal/task are bus task dicts or None.
- Rules, first match wins: kind "retrospective" -> retrospective. kind "scouts_done": ctx.scout_count == 0 -> initial_goal_plan, else scout_results. kind "held": ctx.signature_repeated or ctx.spec_review_request_changes >= 2 or ctx.auto_fix_rounds_used >= ctx.auto_fix_rounds -> architectural_replan; else ctx.failing_ids non-empty or ctx.in_scope_review_comments -> fix_strategy; else held_task. kind "closable" -> closable_goal. Unknown kind -> other. After that, ambiguous_requirement overrides initial_goal_plan/scout_results when the goal text (title + spec) carries ambiguity markers: two or more of the tokens "or", "either", "unclear", "tbd", "?", "conflict", "maybe", "alternatively" (case-insensitive, whole words, "?" counted per occurrence), or ctx.get("ambiguous") is True; signals records which markers fired.
- architectural = attribution.task_class(task or goal) in ("architectural", "security") or (complexity >= 7) or ctx.touches_interfaces or ctx.touches_migrations or decision_type == architectural_replan; use task complexity for held, goal complexity otherwise.
- risk_class: high when ctx.touches_auth or ctx.touches_data_deletion or ctx.security_trigger or task_class == "security"; low when ctx.touches_interfaces or ctx.touches_migrations or ctx.semantic_trigger; else none. Missing ctx fields count as False/0 and add signal "unknown:<field>" (never raise).
- band via attribution.band(complexity); task_class via attribution.task_class(task or goal) guarded so a missing pool.toml never raises (attribution already guards).
- explain(classification) -> one line string "type=... arch=... risk=... signals=a,b".
Docstring states purpose-over-complexity with the example: a complexity 8 closable_goal is routine, a complexity 6 ambiguous_requirement is not.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py::test_held_with_failing_tests_is_fix_strategy — held ctx with failing_ids and no risk flags classifies fix_strategy, architectural False, risk none

tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py::test_repeated_signature_is_architectural_replan — held ctx with signature_repeated True classifies architectural_replan and architectural True regardless of complexity 3
tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py::test_scouts_done_without_scouts_is_initial_goal_plan — scout_count 0 gives initial_goal_plan; scout_count 2 gives scout_results

tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py::test_ambiguity_markers_override_to_ambiguous_requirement — goal spec 'use redis or postgres, unclear which?' classifies ambiguous_requirement with signals naming the markers; a plain spec does not

tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py::test_risk_and_missing_fields_never_raise — touches_auth True gives risk high; a ctx missing every optional field classifies without raising and lists unknown:<field> signals; closable kind gives closable_goal at complexity 8 with architectural True

result.summary: All 5 acceptance tests pass (verified via unittest run). DECISION_TYPES, classify() routing rules, ambiguity-marker detection, risk_class/architectural derivation, and explain() all match the spec's stated formulas. Checked one candidate discrepancy — architectural/task_class uses an entity selected by kind=="held" rather than the spec's literal "task or goal" — but planner_runs' point structure only ever supplies a task_id for kind=="held" (scouts_done/closable key on goal_id alone), so the two formulations are equivalent for every real call site; not a live bug. Missing-ctx fields are defaulted and signaled per spec without raising, guards around attribution.task_class/band hold up under empty/None entities.
